# 3. Experiments (auto-generated by the ML pipeline)

All tables/figures are written to `ml/results/`. Files carry a `data_mode` column (`REAL` or `SYNTHETIC_DEMO`) and demo plots
are watermarked. **Experimental results to be populated after model training on real data — synthetic outputs are never results.**

| # | Question | Script | Outputs |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Which algorithm performs best? | `training/train.py` | `exp1_model_comparison.csv/.png`, `exp1_confusion_matrix.csv/.png` |
| 2 | Contribution of each modality (A keyboard, B mouse, C app, D K+M, E K+M+A, F all + baseline) | `evaluation/run_experiments.py` | `exp2_feature_groups.csv/.png` |
| 3 | Personalised (absolute + deviation) vs generic (absolute only), per model | same | `exp3_personalised_vs_generic.csv/.png` |
| 4 | Which features matter? (impurity, permutation, SHAP) | same | `exp4_*.csv/.png` |
| 5 | Stress trend over sessions | same | `exp5_stress_trend.csv/.png` |

## Interpreting outcomes honestly
* If F ≈ E on real data, the personalised features did not add discriminative power for that cohort — report it, discuss why
  (small calibration set, label noise, participants with stable behaviour).
* Report per-participant variance; N will be small in a student study, so present confidence intervals or fold-wise ranges rather
  than a single decimal.
* The synthetic generator encodes the *assumed* stress effects; high accuracy on it only proves the pipeline works.
